title: Nine Parts Starch
subtitle: 衣饰与配件 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 衣饰与配件（生活与学习·服饰与仪表）
meta: 主题语境：衣饰与配件（生活与学习·服饰与仪表）　|　核心词汇：collar　|　正文 334 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 collar 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 my father ① turned up his collar against the wind on the way to his first office job, and he said the turning was the whole of the morning. The ② collar, meaning the cloth and not the neck, was stiff with starch and stayed that way; collar, he said, is the only thing in a shirt that is judged by how straight it stands.

Every ③ collar in that wardrobe had the same starch, and the ④ collar at the end, meaning the one he kept for interviews and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever ironed twice. Collar, my mother said, is nine parts starch and one part somebody willing to stand straight; my father said the standing is the part that wears out.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ collaring the dog was the whole of the afternoon, meaning the leather and not the cloth. The ⑥ collar, meaning the leather and not any of that, is the only thing in an afternoon that everybody notices and nobody praises; collar, he said, is either something you starch or the only word that means both a cloth and a leather. She said the leather is the part they remember.

By 1975 the ⑦ collar had become a word in an advertisement, and the advertisement had become an argument about class. The ⑧ collar of the whole thing, my father wrote in June, was one shirt and thirty years of standing; collar, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to keep your chin up. He said the chin was never mentioned.

The ⑨ collar I remember is the one at the end, which was starched in 1980 and is still described as the straightest in the street. A ⑩ collar, my mother said in 1982, is the only thing that improves by being worn; every collar, she said, is a class that has agreed to look like a cloth. She said the class was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 衣领（指那件衬衫的领子本身，与那些袖口相对）
C. 固定搭配：turn up one's collar 竖起衣领（挡风）
D. n. 衣领（指那个衣柜里每一道）
E. n. 衣领（指末尾那一道）
F. v. 给……戴上项圈；抓住、揪住（collar the dog）
G. n. 项圈（指那根皮革颈圈，与那块布相对）
H. n. 身份；阶层标记（抽象总称，白领身份）

items.q: turned up his collar against the wind
The collar, meaning the cloth and not the neck
collaring the dog was the whole of the afternoon
the collar had become a word in an advertisement
The collar of the whole thing
A collar, my mother said in 1982

answers.why: turn up one's collar 意为“竖起衣领（挡风）”，1968 年父亲在去第一份办公室工作的路上竖起衣领挡风。
collar 意为“衣领”，指那件衬衫的领子本身而不是脖子，浆得笔挺。
collar 指那个衣柜里每一道衣领，每一道都上着同样的浆。
collar 指末尾那一道（他留着面试穿的那一道），是唯一有人熨过两次的。
collar 作动词，意为“给……戴上项圈；抓住”，叔叔说给狗套项圈就是那个下午的全部。
collar 意为“项圈”，指那根皮革颈圈而不是那块布，是下午里人人留意、却无人称赞的东西。
collar 意为“身份、阶层标记”（白领身份），到 1975 年这道衣领成了广告里的一个词。
collar 意为“衣领”，父亲六月写道，整件事说到底是一件衬衫和三十年的站立。
collar 意为“衣领”，我记得的是末尾那一道，1980 年上过浆，至今仍被说成全街最挺的。
collar 为抽象总称，母亲说一道衣领是唯一会因为被穿而变好的东西。
